scope: Production cleanup scheduling and aggregate health wiring, verified on isolated local API; not production deployment or complete deletion acceptance.
implemented: Repositories initialize anonymization/cleanup repositories; services initialize the cleanup worker with configured upload root. Main starts the worker immediately and every minute, and stops it during graceful shutdown before database teardown.

A second Start shares the existing loop rather than creating another worker. Cancellation, idempotent stop and restart are supported. Each batch uses a thirty-second database context and at most 25 records; local OS filesystem calls themselves are not claimed to be forcibly cancellable.

Mutex-protected aggregate status includes running state, actual last check/success, consecutive incomplete batches and last result. Failed removals or database/root errors report incomplete status without exposing queued URLs or raw local-path errors.

GET /api/health remains HTTP 200 for liveness while reporting degraded cleanup when stopped, unpolled, stale for more than three minutes or failing. No request-time filesystem/database cleanup is performed by health reads.
